subject.title: fix(cli-runner): sweep orphaned bundle MCP temp dirs at gateway startup

question: Is the Linux exact-head proof plus fail-closed handling sufficient for the startup deletion boundary, or must the PR first prove or explicitly guard shared-temp and non-Linux process-visibility cases?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but repository context does not define whether multiple gateways may share a temporary root across PID namespaces; that support boundary determines whether the remaining availability risk is acceptable.

options.title: Refresh and accept bounded risk
options.body: Rebase onto current main, require related checks to pass, and land the fail-closed design with shared-temp PID-namespace isolation treated as unsupported unless separately proven.

options.title: Require broader process proof
options.body: Hold merge until macOS or Windows and shared-temp concurrent-gateway scenarios demonstrate that live queued configurations cannot be reclaimed.

options.title: Pause for namespace-safe ownership
options.body: Replace PID-relative ownership with an identity or temp-root ownership scheme that remains unambiguous across isolated process namespaces.

recommendation.title: Refresh and accept bounded risk
recommendation.body: Rebase onto current main, require related checks to pass, and land the fail-closed design with shared-temp PID-namespace isolation treated as unsupported unless separately proven.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged live-session cleanup work is the strongest available history signal for the bundle-MCP lifecycle invariant, though final authority should come from a current repository owner.
